about: API-3 scope (API-STANDARD S33-S36). Curated by cb-api with the owning area. money_writes: routes that move or record money; each must require an Idempotency-Key. inbound: routes that take a peer's or a webhook's JSON; each must schema-check it before use. money_reviewed_not: routes whose path looks like money but that write nothing (a preview, a build). public_ids: routes whose path value S35 does not apply to, each with its reason: public by design (a public door, a counterparty door, platform reference), or a label or reference that names nothing outside the caller's own shop (a fiscal year, a per-shop reference); foreign_id_404 (S35) does not apply to them. tools/api-register.cjs --check fails when a mutating route that looks like money is in none of the lists.

public_ids.POST /api/catalogue/enquiry/:item_id: counterparty door: an enquiry is a business asking about ANOTHER business's published item, which rings that owner's bell (sec4 C); another shop's item id answering is the purpose (API-24, 2026-11-01)

public_ids.POST /api/governance/boilerplate/:key/ad: platform reference: the key names the platform's boilerplate; the adoption is written to the caller's own shop
public_ids.GET /api/governance/source/:key: platform reference: a catalogue source is shared by every shop it serves
public_ids.GET /api/governance/readiness/:bridge_id: counterparty door: the readiness passport is built for outsiders (Athi 2026-08-20); a stranger gets status and rung only, evidence_ref stripped (SEC-FIX3 S6)
public_ids.GET /api/assist/container/:id: platform reference: a container is shared catalogue reference that chits pin by version
public_ids.POST /api/integrations/ask/:handle/stock: public door: a shop's published handle answers stock to an asking peer
public_ids.GET /api/integrations/stock/:handle: public door: a shop's published handle answers stock to an asking peer
public_ids.PUT /api/folders/inventory/:code: platform reference: the code names a system folder of the platform's inventory (lib/folder-inventory: B-2100, RT-4090 …), the same in every shop; the switch is written to the caller's own policy
public_ids.GET /api/books/year/:fy/status: label: a fiscal-year label, the same in every shop; read only inside the caller's own periods (WHERE entity_id = $1), no path from the label to a row id (lib/books-store periods)
public_ids.POST /api/books/year/:fy/close: label: a fiscal-year label, the same in every shop; it acts only on the caller's own periods (setPeriodStatus names entity_id = $1)
public_ids.POST /api/books/periods/:fy/:p/:act: label: a fiscal-year label, a period number and an action word, the same in every shop; the UPDATE names the caller's entity (lib/books-store setPeriodStatus)
public_ids.POST /api/books/loans/:ref/emi: per-shop reference: loan:<ref> is the entry's source_ref, typed by the owner and unique inside one shop; looked up only with entity_id = $1, refused before any write when absent
public_ids.POST /api/books/accruals/:ref/reverse: per-shop reference: accrual:<ref> is the entry's source_ref, typed by the owner and unique inside one shop; looked up only with entity_id = $1, refused before any write when absent
public_ids.GET /api/assist/catalogue-source/:key: platform reference: the key names a catalogue source shared by every shop, not a row of any shop (routes/assist.js)
public_ids.GET /api/catalogue/:bridge_id/my-documen: public door family: the path id is the shop browsed, as GET /api/catalogue/:bridge_id; the read is the caller's own documents under it (entity_id of the caller)
public_ids.GET /api/catalogue/:bridge_id/my-orders: public door family: the path id is the shop browsed, as GET /api/catalogue/:bridge_id; the read is the caller's own orders under it (entity_id of the caller)
public_ids.GET /api/catalogue/enquiry/:item_id: counterparty door: an enquiry list is the caller's own, under another business's published item; the empty list is the answer (as POST /api/catalogue/enquiry/:item_id)
public_ids.GET /api/facts/:card: platform reference: the id is a card name of the facts engine, not a row of any shop
public_ids.GET /api/forms/:key: platform reference: the key names a form template, shared reference data the same in every shop
public_ids.GET /api/governance/supplier-acceptance/: counterparty door: the handle is a public directory bridge id; an unknown handle answers 200 null by design (routes/governance.js)
public_ids.GET /api/integrations/docs/:id: platform reference: the id names a connector-kit catalogue entry, the same for every shop
public_ids.GET /api/integrations/download/:id: platform reference: the id names a connector-kit catalogue entry, the same for every shop
public_ids.GET /api/products/media/:item_id/:mid: public door: product media is served by unguessable ids, public by design (routes/products.js)
public_ids.GET /api/till/engine/:name: platform reference: the name is an engine file of the till, not a row of any shop
public_ids.PATCH /api/entities/me/prefs/:kind: label: the kind is a preference name on the caller's own row, the same in every shop
public_ids.POST /api/forms/:key/issue: platform reference: the key names a form template, shared reference data the same in every shop; the issue is written to the caller's own shop
public_ids.PUT /api/identity/documents/:scheme: label: the scheme names a kind of document for the shop's own country (PAN, GSTIN, ABN), shared reference data, not a row of any shop; an unknown scheme answers 400 by design (routes/identity-docs.js)
public_ids.POST /api/forms/:key/resolve: platform reference: the key names a form template, shared reference data the same in every shop
public_ids.GET /api/chits/:chit_id/catalogue-overla: label: the chit id is not read by the handler; the overlay is the caller's own catalogue (itemmatch.loadCatalogue by entity), so the path value names no row of any shop

platform_only_about: platform_only: routes only the platform (admin key, rootGate, platformGate) or the builder can call, each with its reason. They are NOT public: no shop ever reaches the id, so foreign_id_404 (S35) does not apply, exactly as for public_ids. Read by tools/api-register.cjs hardeningScope; tools/api-register.cjs --check holds the same rules as public_ids (reason of 20+ characters, a route that exists).

platform_only.PATCH /api/entities/:id/erase: platform only: platformGate refuses every shop before the id is read, so a shop never reaches it
platform_only.POST /api/channels/:id/approve: platform only: the admin gate (platform key) refuses every shop before the id is read
platform_only.POST /api/channels/:id/revoke: platform only: the admin gate (platform key) refuses every shop before the id is read
platform_only.POST /api/channels/:id/template-approve: platform only: the admin gate (platform key) refuses every shop before the id is read
platform_only.POST /api/governance/entities/:id/reatte: platform only: platformGate refuses every shop (403) before the id is read; the route's own 404 paths are tested as the platform caller in api-problem-governance
platform_only.PUT /api/entities/populations/:code/desk: platform only: rootGate refuses every shop; the code names a population, not a row of a shop
platform_only.PUT /api/testing/cmdb/:ci: builder only: the ci is a configuration-item name on the testing board's own entity, never a shop's row

cannot_answer_about: error_tests exemption (API-STANDARD S33-S38, critic 6 Nov 2026 section 5): a status a route declares (the register implies 404 on every route with a : in its path, and 500 on every route) but can never answer, so no test can ever show it. Each entry names a route, the status and the reason; reviewed by cb-api. Read only by the error_tests column; status_codes is judged as before.

tolerant_outward_about: API-43: keyed-outward doors that ignore an unknown body key until a /v2 path with notice. The register reads strict_input as exempt (never yes), only while the route still checks the fields it reads. The length may only go down (tools/api-ratchet.cjs).
